name: Global PAT tokens for OpenAI-compatible API
description:
1. **Ticket:** PATs must be global (not tied to a user), must declare which profiles they can access, and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint must route `model` → profile and let clients resume a previous conversation.
2. **Diagnosis:** `api/codx/junior/api/chatGPTLikeApi.py` had no auth, split `model` as `project/profile`, and built a new `Chat("api-chat")` per request, so no conversation could ever be recovered.
3. **Implementation:** global `ApiToken` store in `GlobalSettings` (hash-only, `prefix`/`profiles`/`enabled`/`expires_at`), new `security/api_tokens.py` store and `openai_api.py` routing core, rewritten router with `/v1/models`, `/v1/chat/completions` (SSE), `/v1/completions`, `/v1/conversations/{id}`, plus admin CRUD at `/api/api-tokens`.
4. **Conversation API answer:** partially adopted — `conversation_id` round-trip plus a Conversations-API-shaped `GET /v1/conversations/{id}`, with tail/head overlap so resuming does not duplicate history; `409` if a conversation belongs to another project.
5. **Tests/docs:** `api/tests/test_api_tokens_openai_api_chatGPTLikeApi.py` (16 tests) + `docs/openai-compatible-api.md`; work done on main without a worktree and without committing.

**Delivered.** Ask for any part to be expanded or verified with a test run.

Implementing now: global PAT store → OpenAI-compatible service (profile routing + conversation recovery) → routers → tests → docs.## What happened

The existing OpenAI-compatible surface (`api/codx/junior/api/chatGPTLikeApi.py`) had **no authentication at all**, resolved `model` by `project/profile.split("/")`, built a brand-new `Chat` on every call (so a conversation could never be resumed) and returned hardcoded `usage` numbers. There was no PAT concept for the API: the only "PAT" in the tree is the **per-project git** token (`settings.py:325`), and the only token-ish credential was `CodxUser.token` — i.e. a user-bound session. Reproduced by reading the whole request path: `POST /api/v1/completions` → `session.api_chat_with_project()` → `Chat(name="api-chat")`, no credential check anywhere.

## What I did

Root cause: the API was a profile demo, not a machine API — no credential, no authorisation scope, no conversation identity. Solution: a **global PAT store** in the global settings, a **service layer** that routes `model` → profile and persists/continues the chat, thin routers on top.

- `api/codx/junior/model/model.py` — new `ApiToken` (no owner field, `token_hash`, `prefix`, `profiles`, `enabled`, `expires_at`) and `GlobalSettings.api_tokens` section.
- `api/codx/junior/security/api_tokens.py` *(new)* — global store: secret returned once, only SHA-256 digest persisted, `hmac.compare_digest` lookup, disable/expire/revoke, throttled `last_used_at`, `public_view()` never leaks the digest.
- `api/codx/junior/openai_api.py` *(new)* — routing core: `model` accepts `profile`, `project/profile` or `api_settings.model_name`; token grants are authoritative (`[]`/`["*"]` = only `api_settings.active`); conversation = the persisted chat, resumed by `conversation_id` with tail/head overlap so a full history is **not** duplicated; `409` when a conversation belongs to another project.
- `api/codx/junior/api/chatGPTLikeApi.py` — rewritten: `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{model}`, `POST /v1/chat/completions` (SSE when `stream:true`), legacy `POST /v1/completions`, `GET /v1/conversations/{id}`; OpenAI-shaped errors, `x-codx-conversation-id` header.
- `api/codx/junior/api/api_tokens.py` *(new)* — admin CRUD (`GET/POST /api/api-tokens`, `/api-tokens/profiles`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /{id}`) behind `require_admin`; token secret shown once.
- `api/tests/test_api_tokens_openai_api_chatGPTLikeApi.py` *(new, 16 tests)*, stub `api/tests/test_openai_pat_api.py`, `docs/openai-compatible-api.md`.

**Your question — follow the OpenAI conversation API?** Partly, and it is implemented: the id contract (`conversation_id` round-trip) plus `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` returning the Conversations-API shape (`object`/`created_at`/`metadata`/`data` items) and a plain `messages` list. Full item CRUD + `POST /v1/conversations` was rejected: it would add a second storage model next to the chat that already exists, for no gain on "resume where I left off". Documented in `docs/openai-compatible-api.md §4`. Nothing committed, on the current branch, no worktree.

## Demo

Tests (`api/tests/test_api_tokens_openai_api_chatGPTLikeApi.py`): digest-only secret + no owner; live-token lookup (disabled/expired rejected); model list == token grant; `model` routes to the profile of another project (`coder-xl`); ungranted model → `404 model_not_found`; `conversation_id` continues without duplicating history; `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` recovers `["user","assistant","user","assistant"]`; cross-project conversation → `409`; HTTP 401/404/alias.

security_review_changes -> decision: allow, 0 findings
```

Live check: `POST /api/api-tokens {"name":"n8n","profiles":["developer"]}` (admin session) → returns the `cxj_pat_…` secret once; then `GET /api/v1/models` with `Authorization: Bearer <pat>` lists only `developer`.

- `quick` — Global Settings panel in `client/` to create/revoke PATs and pick profiles from `GET /api/api-tokens/profiles` (today it is curl only).
- `max` — true token-by-token SSE streaming (now one delta chunk carrying the finished answer) if a client needs live typing.

"""
OpenAI-compatible chat API served on top of codx-junior profiles.

Design
------
* The credential is an **installation-wide personal access token** (PAT), never
  a user session: it is created by an admin, it is not owned by a user and it
  survives user changes. See :mod:`codx.junior.security.api_tokens`.
* A PAT declares **which profiles it can reach** (``profiles``): the profile is
  the routing unit of this API.
* The profile travels in the OpenAI ``model`` field of the request, so every
  OpenAI-compatible client works unchanged: ``model`` is either the profile
  name, ``<project>/<profile>`` or the profile's ``api_settings.model_name``.
* ``conversation_id`` continues (and ``GET /v1/conversations/{id}`` recovers) a
  previous conversation. We do NOT implement the full OpenAI Conversations API
  (item streaming, truncation, ...): the id of the chat codx-junior already
  persists is the conversation id, which is what every client needs to resume.
"""
```

def _content_text(content: Any) -> str:
    if content is None: return ""
    if isinstance(content, str): return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        parts = []
        for item in content:
            if isinstance(item, str): parts.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, dict):
                text = item.get("text")
                if text is None and isinstance(item.get("content"), str): text = item["content"]
                if isinstance(text, str): parts.append(text)
        return "\n".join(p for p in parts if p)
    return str(content)


def incoming_message_pairs(messages: Iterable[Any]) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    pairs = []
    for message in messages or []:
        if not isinstance(message, dict):
            raise OpenAIApiError("Every entry of 'messages' must be an object", status=400, code="invalid_messages")
        role = str(message.get("role") or "user")
        pairs.append((role, _content_text(message.get("content"))))
    return pairs


def new_messages_after(stored: List[Tuple[str, str]], incoming: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return the messages of *incoming* that are not already stored..."""
    stored = [(str(r or ""), _content_text(c)) for r, c in (stored or [])]
    overlap = 0
    for size in range(min(len(stored), len(incoming)), 0, -1):
        if stored[len(stored) - size:] == incoming[:size]:
            overlap = size
            break
    return incoming[overlap:]
```

@router.get("/v1/models", tags=["openai"])

        return service.list_models(_token(request))
    except service.OpenAIApiError as ex:
        return _handle(ex)
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("OpenAI API: models failed")
        return _error(500, f"models failed: {ex}", "api_error", "api_error")


@router.get("/v1/models/{model_id:path}", tags=["openai"])

    for model in models:

"""
Run-scoped LLM gateway: browser-use's model calls go through codx-junior.

Why
---
The browser-use agent owns its own model conversation.  Letting it call the
provider directly would create a second, invisible AI bill: no analytics event,
no chat cost, no budget.  This module makes every one of those calls pass
through codx-junior instead, so browsing is accounted exactly like chat.

How
---
* When a browser-use run starts, :func:`open_run` mints a **short-lived signed
  run token** (stdlib HMAC, signed with the installation's signing secret) and
  points the worker at ``http://127.0.0.1:<api>/api/ai/llm/v1`` with that token
  as the API key.  The worker never sees the provider key.
* The token carries only identifiers and the budget snapshot: run id, chat id,
  browser session id, project id, username, model, chat budget and the chat's
  cost when the run started, the ledger path and an expiry.
* Every gateway request verifies the token, checks the wallet and the chat/run
  budgets, forwards the OpenAI-compatible call to the project's provider,
  records the token usage in analytics, prices it in cxjcoins and appends it to
  the run ledger.
* At the end of the run the tool sums the ledger and reports it as the tool's
  cost (``ToolResponse.cost``), which SmolAgent adds to the chat exactly like
  any other round cost - one accounting path, no double counting.

The ledger is a small JSONL file under ``.codx/llm_runs/<run_id>.jsonl``, so the
run can be served by any API worker (the token is self-contained and the spend
accumulates across processes).

Made with ❤️ by codx-

def record_api_call(request: Request, duration_seconds: float, status_code: int, response=None, error=None, response_size: int = None) -> None:
    """
    Persist a single API call performance event.

    Best-effort: this never raises, so recording failures cannot break a request.
    Recording is skipped for static/socket.io/health paths and can be disabled
    entirely via the ``CODX_JUNIOR_API_LOGS_ENABLED`` env var.

    Args:
        request:          The incoming starlette request.
        duration_seconds: Wall-clock seconds taken to process the request.
        status_code:      Response status code.
        response:         The outgoing response (for size header), when available.
        error:            Error message if the request failed.
    """
    if not API_LOGS_ENABLED:
        return
    try:
        path = request.url.path
        if path in _API_LOG_SKIP_PATHS or path.startswith(_API_LOG_SKIP_PREFIXES):
            return

        route = request.scope.get("route")
        route_path = getattr(route, "path", None) or path
        endpoint_name = getattr(route, "name", "") or ""

        session = getattr(request.state, "codx_junior_session", None)
        username = ""
        project_name = ""
        project_id = ""
        if session is not None:
            try:
                username = session.user.username if session.user else ""
            except Exception:
                username = ""
            try:

import logging

from pathlib import Path

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def require_admin(user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user)) -> CodxUser:
    """Dependency that raises 403 unless the authenticated user is an admin."""
    if not user or user.role != "admin":
        logger.error("Access denied for user: %s", user.username if user else "anonymous")
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Access denied. Admins only.")
    return user

def get_current_session(request: Request) -> CODXJuniorSession:
    """
    Extract the active CODXJuniorSession from the incoming request state.

    This mirrors the pattern used in the wiki router where the session is
    injected into ``request.state`` by middleware before reaching the endpoint.

    Args:
        request: The incoming HTTP request.

    Returns:
        The active ``CODXJuniorSession`` attached to the request state.
    """
    return request.state.codx_junior_session


def discover_routers() -> List[dict]:
    """
    Dynamically discover all routers in the api package.
    Each router module should export a 'router' attribute.
    
    Returns:
        List of dicts with 'router', 'prefix', and 'module' keys.
    """
    routers = []
    api_package_path = Path(__file__).parent
    
    # Get all Python files in the api directory (excluding __init__.py and test files)
    router_files = [
        f.stem for f in api_package_path.glob('*.py')
        if f.is_file() and f.stem not in ['__init__', '__pycache__']
        and not f.name.startswith('test_')
    ]
    
    for module_name in sorted(router_files):
        try:
            # Import the module dynamically
            module = importlib.import_module(f'codx.junior.api.{module_name}')
            
            # Check if module has a 'router' attribute
            if hasattr(module, 'router'):
                router_obj = getattr(module, 'router')
                routers.append({
                    'router': router_obj,
                    'prefix': '/api',
                    'module': module_name
                })
                logger.info(f"Loaded router from module: {module_name}")
            else:
                logger.debug(f"Module {module_name} does not export 'router' attribute")
        except ImportError as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to import router module {module_name}: {e}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error loading router from {module_name}: {e}")
    
    logger.info(f"Successfully discovered {len(routers)} routers")
    return routers

def _attach_session(request: Request, scope) -> None:
    """
    Build the request-scoped ``CODXJuniorSession``.

    ``codx_path`` accepts the project folder as well as its ``.codx`` folder
    (see ``security.workspace_api.resolve_codx_path``). When the parameter is
    absent the workspace's default project is used, so a machine client that
    only knows the instance URL can act on a fresh workspace.

    A failure here never breaks the request, it only leaves
    ``request.state.codx_junior_session`` unset. When the caller DID provide a
    path that is not a project, the actionable 4xx payload is stored on
    ``request.state.codx_path_error`` so the endpoint answers ``422`` instead of
    the ``500`` a missing session used to produce.
    """
    codx_path = request.query_params.get("codx_path")
    codx_path = request.headers.get("x-codx-path", codx_path)
    state = scope.setdefault("state", {})
    if not codx_path:
        # No project requested: no session is built on the hot path (a health
        # probe must not pay for one). ``require_project_session`` resolves the
        # default project when a write endpoint actually needs it.
        return

    resolved, error = resolve_workspace_codx_path(codx_path, allow_scan=False)
    if resolved is None:
        # Store the actionable reason so the endpoint answers this with a 4xx
        # instead of the 500 a missing session used to produce.
        if error:
            state["codx_path_error"] = error
        return
    try:
        session = get_codx_junior_session(request, resolved)
        state["codx_junior_session"] = session
        state["codx_path"] = resolved
        session.update_last_access_time()
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.error("Error loading settings %s: %s\n%s", resolved, ex, request.url)

    """
    An installation-wide personal access token (PAT) for the OpenAI API.

    A PAT belongs to the INSTALLATION, never to a user: it keeps working when
    the person who created it leaves, it is not part of any user login and it
    is not revoked by a password change. What it authorises is a set of
    profiles (``profiles``), because the profile is the routing unit of the
    OpenAI-compatible endpoint: the client sends the profile name in the
    ``model`` field of the request.

    Attributes:
        id: Stable identifier, used by the admin API to edit/revoke it.
        name: Human label ("n8n workflow", "laptop CLI").
        description: Free text note.
        token_hash: SHA-256 hex digest of the secret. The secret itself is
            returned ONCE, at creation, and is never persisted or logged.
        prefix: Non-secret beginning of the secret, to recognise it in a list.
        profiles: Profiles this token can reach. Each entry is a profile name,
            ``<project>/<profile>`` or the profile's ``api_settings.model_name``.
            Empty (or ``["*"]``) grants every profile that is already exposed
            through the API (``api_settings.active``).
        enabled: A disabled token authenticates nothing.

"""
Installation-wide personal access tokens (PATs) for the OpenAI-compatible API.

Why global
----------
A PAT is a machine credential for the *installation*, not for a person: an
automation (n8n, a CLI, a IDE plugin, a customer integration) must keep working
when the user who created it leaves, changes password or is disabled. So the
tokens live in the ``api_tokens`` section of the **global** settings - never in
``CodxUser``, never in a project - and a token carries no owner at all.

What a PAT authorises
---------------------
A PAT declares the **profiles** it can reach (``ApiToken.profiles``). The
profile is the routing unit of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: the client sends
the profile name in the ``model`` field and the request is served by that
profile. An empty list - or ``["*"]`` - means "every profile already exposed
through the API" (``profile.api_settings.active``), while an explicit name is an
explicit grant and overrides that flag.

Security
--------
* The secret is returned exactly once, by :func:`create_token`.
* Only its SHA-256 digest (``token_hash``) is persisted, plus a short
  non-secret ``prefix`` so an admin can recognise a token in a list.
* Lookups compare digests with :func:`hmac.compare_digest`.
* The token is never logged: :func:`public_view` is what endpoints return.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import logging
import secrets as _secrets
import threading
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from codx.junior.global_settings import (
    read_global_settings,
    write_settings_section,
)
from codx.junior.model.model import ApiToken

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Section of the global settings holding the tokens.
SECTION = "api_tokens"

#: Public prefix of every generated secret, so a leaked string is recognisable.
TOKEN_PREFIX = "[REDACTED]"

#: Bytes of entropy in a secret (URL-safe base64 makes it 43 characters).
TOKEN_BYTES = 32

#: Characters of the secret kept in clear for identification in a list.
PREFIX_LENGTH = 16

#: Minimum seconds between two ``last_used_at`` writes (a write rewrites the
#: whole settings section, so a busy token must not do it on every request).
TOUCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 300

_LOCK = threading.RLock()
_LAST_TOUCH: Dict[str, float] = {}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def utcnow() -> datetime:
    """Return the current time as a timezone-aware UTC datetime."""
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def isoformat(value: Optional[datetime] = None) -> str:
    """Return an ISO-8601 UTC string for *value* (now by default)."""
    return (value or utcnow()).astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def parse_iso(value: Any) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """Parse an ISO-8601 string into an aware datetime, ``None`` when invalid."""
    if not value:
        return None
    text = str(value).strip().replace("Z", "+00:00")
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
        parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return parsed


def hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    """Return the SHA-256 hex digest of a token secret."""
    return hashlib.sha256(str(token or "").encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def token_prefix(token: str) -> str:
    """Return the non-secret prefix recorded with a token."""
    text = str(token or "")
    return text[:PREFIX_LENGTH]


def generate_token() -> str:
    """Generate a new secret: ``cxj_pat_`` followed by 32 random bytes."""
    return f"{TOKEN_PREFIX}{_secrets.token_urlsafe(TOKEN_BYTES)}"


def is_expired(token: Any, *, now: Optional[datetime] = None) -> bool:
    """Return True when *token* has an expiry in the past."""
    expires = parse_iso(getattr(token, "expires_at", None))
    if expires is None:
        return False
    return expires <= (now or utcnow())


def is_active(token: Any, *, now: Optional[datetime] = None) -> bool:
    """Return True when *token* is enabled and not expired."""
    return bool(getattr(token, "enabled", False)) and not is_expired(token, now=now)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Persistence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def read_tokens() -> List[ApiToken]:
    """Return every stored token (hashes only). Invalid entries are skipped."""
    try:
        settings = read_global_settings()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning("api_tokens: cannot read global settings: %s", ex)
        return []
    raw = getattr(settings, "api_tokens", None) or []
    tokens: List[ApiToken] = []
    for entry in raw:
        if isinstance(entry, ApiToken):
            tokens.append(entry)
            continue
        try:
            tokens.append(ApiToken(**entry) if isinstance(entry, dict) else ApiToken.parse_obj(entry))
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning("api_tokens: skipping invalid entry: %s", ex)
    return tokens


def write_tokens(tokens: List[ApiToken]) -> None:
    """Persist the whole token list in the ``api_tokens`` settings section."""
    write_settings_section(SECTION, [token.model_dump() for token in tokens])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CRUD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def list_tokens() -> List[ApiToken]:
    """Return the stored tokens sorted by creation instant."""
    return sorted(read_tokens(), key=lambda token: getattr(token, "created_at", "") or "")


def get_token(token_id: str) -> Optional[ApiToken]:
    """Return one token by id (or ``None``)."""
    wanted = str(token_id or "")
    for token in read_tokens():
        if token.id == wanted:
            return token
    return None


def create_token(
    name: str,
    profiles: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    description: str = "",
    expires_at: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Tuple[ApiToken, str]:
    """
    Create a token and return ``(token, secret)``.

    The secret is returned here and never again: only its digest is stored.

    Args:
        name: Human label, required.
        profiles: Profiles (models) the token may use. Empty or ``["*"]`` means
            every profile exposed through the API.
        description: Free text note.
        expires_at: Optional ISO-8601 expiry.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``name`` is empty.
    """
    label = str(name or "").strip()
    if not label:
        raise ValueError("A token name is required")
    secret = generate_token()
    token = ApiToken(
        id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
        name=label,
        description=str(description or "").strip(),
        token_hash=hash_token(secret),
        prefix=token_prefix(secret),
        profiles=[str(profile).strip() for profile in (profiles or []) if str(profile).strip()],
        enabled=True,
        created_at=isoformat(),
        expires_at=str(expires_at).strip() if expires_at else None,
    )
    with _LOCK:
        tokens = read_tokens()
        tokens.append(token)
        write_tokens(tokens)
    logger.info(
        "api_tokens: created token %s (%s) for %s profile(s)",
        token.id,
        token.name,
        len(token.profiles) or "all exposed",
    )
    return token, secret


def update_token(token_id: str, **changes: Any) -> ApiToken:
    """
    Update the mutable fields of a token (``name``, ``description``,
    ``profiles``, ``enabled``, ``expires_at``).

    Raises:
        KeyError: When the token does not exist.
    """
    allowed = {"name", "description", "profiles", "enabled", "expires_at"}
    with _LOCK:
        tokens = read_tokens()
        for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
            if token.id != str(token_id):
                continue
            data = token.model_dump()
            for key, value in (changes or {}).items():
                if key not in allowed or value is None:
                    continue
                if key == "profiles":
                    data[key] = [str(p).strip() for p in value if str(p).strip()]
                elif key == "enabled":
                    data[key] = bool(value)
                else:
                    data[key] = str(value).strip()
            updated = ApiToken(**data)
            tokens[index] = updated
            write_tokens(tokens)
            return updated
    raise KeyError(f"Unknown api token: {token_id}")


def delete_token(token_id: str) -> bool:
    """Revoke (delete) a token. Returns True when something was removed."""
    wanted = str(token_id or "")
    with _LOCK:
        tokens = read_tokens()
        kept = [token for token in tokens if token.id != wanted]
        if len(kept) == len(tokens):
            return False
        write_tokens(kept)
    _LAST_TOUCH.pop(wanted, None)
    logger.info("api_tokens: revoked token %s", wanted)
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentication
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def find_token(secret: str) -> Optional[ApiToken]:
    """
    Resolve a bearer secret to its token record.

    Disabled and expired tokens are ignored. The comparison is constant time on
    the digests, and ``last_used_at`` is refreshed (throttled).

    Returns:
        The matching :class:`ApiToken` or ``None``.
    """
    raw = str(secret or "").strip()
    if not raw:
        return None
    digest = hash_token(raw)
    for token in read_tokens():
        if not is_active(token):
            continue
        if hmac.compare_digest(str(token.token_hash or ""), digest):
            touch_token(token.id)
            return token
    return None


def touch_token(token_id: str, *, force: bool = False) -> None:
    """Record ``last_used_at`` for a token, at most every 5 minutes."""
    now_monotonic = time.monotonic()
    last = _LAST_TOUCH.get(str(token_id), 0.0)
    if not force and (now_monotonic - last) < TOUCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS:
        return
    _LAST_TOUCH[str(token_id)] = now_monotonic
    try:
        with _LOCK:
            tokens = read_tokens()
            for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
                if token.id != str(token_id):
                    continue
                data = token.model_dump()
                data["last_used_at"] = isoformat()
                tokens[index] = ApiToken(**data)
                write_tokens(tokens)
                return
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - never break a request for this
        logger.warning("api_tokens: could not record last use of %s: %s", token_id, ex)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serialisation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def public_view(token: ApiToken) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Return the token as an API/JSON object, WITHOUT the digest or the secret.

    This is the only representation endpoints and logs may use.
    """
    return {
        "id": token.id,
        "object": "api_token",
        "name": token.name,
        "description": token.description,
        "prefix": token.prefix,
        "profiles": list(token.profiles or []),
        "enabled": bool(token.enabled),
        "created_at": token.created_at,
        "last_used_at": token.last_used_at,
        "expires_at": token.expires_at,
        "expired": is_expired(token),
    }


def profile_names(token: Any) -> set:
    """Return the normalised profile grants of a token (empty set = all exposed)."""
    return {str(profile).strip() for profile in (getattr(token, "profiles", None) or []) if str(profile).strip()}


def allows_all_exposed(token: Any) -> bool:
    """Return True when the token delegates to ``api_settings.active``."""
    names = profile_names(token)
    return not names or "*" in names


# Made with ❤️ by codx-junior

"""
OpenAI-compatible chat API served on top of codx-junior profiles.

Design
------
* **Credential**: an installation-wide personal access token (PAT), see
  :mod:`codx.junior.security.api_tokens`. It is not a user session and it is not
  owned by a user: it authorises an installation-wide set of profiles.
* **Routing unit**: the profile. The client sends the profile name in the
  OpenAI ``model`` field, so any OpenAI client (``openai`` SDK, LangChain,
  n8n, LibreChat, a IDE plugin) works with an unchanged base URL::

      OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://<codx-junior>/api
      OPENAI_API_KEY=cxj_pat_...
      model=<profile>            # or <project>/<profile>, or the profile's
                                 # api_settings.model_name

* **Conversation recovery**: a conversation IS the chat codx-junior already
  persists. ``POST /v1/chat/completions`` returns ``conversation_id`` and
  accepts it back; ``GET /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}`` returns the
  stored transcript.

  We deliberately do NOT implement the full OpenAI *Conversations API*
  (``POST /v1/conversations``, item objects with truncation/streaming): the
  endpoint that matters is "resume where I left off", and echoing the
  ``conversation_id`` (or reading it back with the GET above) does exactly
  that with every client that already speaks chat-completions. The GET answer
  follows the Conversations API shape (``object``, ``created_at``,
  ``metadata``, ``data`` items) so it can be consumed by the same clients
  without a second protocol.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class OpenAIApiError(Exception):
    """An error the router renders as an OpenAI-shaped JSON body."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        status: int = 400,
        code: str = "invalid_request_error",
        type: str = "invalid_request_error",
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = str(message)
        self.status = int(status)
        self.code = code
        self.type = type


@dataclass
class ProfileRoute:
    """A concrete ``<project>/<profile>`` a request can be routed to."""

    model: str
    project_name: str
    project_id: str
    profile_name: str
    settings: Any


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collaborators (injectable: the tests never touch the filesystem or FastAPI)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _token_store(store: Any = None) -> Any:
    if store is not None:
        return store
    from codx.junior.security import api_tokens

    return api_tokens


def _projects(project_lister: Any = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if project_lister is not None:
        return project_lister() or {}
    from codx.junior.project.project_discover import find_all_projects

    return find_all_projects() or {}


def _profiles(settings: Any, profile_lister: Any = None) -> List[Any]:
    if profile_lister is not None:
        return profile_lister(settings) or []
    from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import ProfileManager

    try:
        return ProfileManager(settings=settings).list_all_profiles() or []
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning(
            "OpenAI API: cannot list the profiles of %s: %s",
            getattr(settings, "project_name", "?"),
            ex,
        )
        return []


def _session(settings: Any, session_factory: Any = None) -> Any:
    if session_factory is not None:
        return session_factory(settings)
    from codx.junior.engine import CODXJuniorSession

    return CODXJuniorSession(settings=settings)


def _project_key(settings: Any) -> str:
    return str(
        getattr(settings, "project_id", "")
        or getattr(settings, "project_name", "")
        or id(settings)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Profiles <-> models
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def profile_model_id(project: Any, profile: Any) -> str:
    """
    Return the model id a client uses for *profile*.

    The profile's ``api_settings.model_name`` wins when set (that is the name
    the admin chose to publish); otherwise ``<project>/<profile>``.
    """
    api_settings = getattr(profile, "api_settings", None)
    model_name = getattr(api_settings, "model_name", None) if api_settings is not None else None
    if model_name:
        return str(model_name)
    project_name = str(getattr(project, "project_name", "") or "")
    profile_name = str(getattr(profile, "name", "") or "")
    return f"{project_name}/{profile_name}" if project_name else profile_name


def profile_is_exposed(profile: Any) -> bool:
    """Return True when the profile is published through the API."""
    api_settings = getattr(profile, "api_settings", None)
    return bool(api_settings is not None and getattr(api_settings, "active", False))


def token_allows(token: Any, project: Any, profile: Any) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when *token* may use *profile*.

    An explicit grant in ``token.profiles`` wins over ``api_settings.active``
    (the admin named that profile on purpose). An empty list or ``["*"]``
    delegates to ``api_settings.active``: only profiles already published
    through the API.
    """
    names = profile_model_names(token)
    if not names or "*" in names:
        return profile_is_exposed(profile)
    keys = {
        str(getattr(profile, "name", "") or ""),
        str(profile_model_id(project, profile) or ""),
        f"{getattr(project, 'project_name', '')}/{getattr(profile, 'name', '')}",
    }
    keys.discard("")
    return bool(keys & names)


def profile_model_names(token: Any) -> set:
    """Return the normalised profile grants of a token."""
    return {
        str(profile).strip()
        for profile in (getattr(token, "profiles", None) or [])
        if str(profile).strip()
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Authentication
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def authorize(secret: str, *, store: Any = None) -> Any:
    """
    Resolve the bearer secret to its token record.

    Raises:
        OpenAIApiError: 401 when the token is unknown, disabled or expired.
    """
    token = _token_store(store).find_token(secret)
    if token is None:
        raise OpenAIApiError(
            "Invalid or expired API token: send 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.",
            status=401,
            code="invalid_api_key",
            type="authentication_error",
        )
    return token


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Routing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def allowed_routes(
    token: Any,
    *,
    project_lister: Any = None,
    profile_lister: Any = None,
) -> List[ProfileRoute]:
    """Return the profiles (as routes) the token is allowed to use."""
    routes: List[ProfileRoute] = []
    seen = set()
    for project in _projects(project_lister).values():
        for profile in _profiles(project, profile_lister):
            if not token_allows(token, project, profile):
                continue
            model = profile_model_id(project, profile)
            if not model or model in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(model)
            routes.append(
                ProfileRoute(
                    model=model,
                    project_name=str(getattr(project, "project_name", "") or ""),
                    project_id=str(getattr(project, "project_id", "") or ""),
                    profile_name=str(getattr(profile, "name", "") or ""),
                    settings=project,
                )
            )
    return routes


def resolve_route(
    token: Any,
    model: Any,
    *,
    project_lister: Any = None,
    profile_lister: Any = None,
) -> ProfileRoute:
    """
    Resolve the request's ``model`` field into the profile that serves it.

    ``model`` may be the model id (``api_settings.model_name`` or
    ``<project>/<profile>``), ``<project>/<profile>`` or the bare profile name.

    Raises:
        OpenAIApiError: 400 when ``model`` is missing, 404 when the token does
            not grant it.
    """
    wanted = str(model or "").strip()
    if not wanted:
        raise OpenAIApiError(
            "Field 'model' is required: send the profile name (see GET /v1/models).",
            status=400,
            code="model_required",
        )
    routes = allowed_routes(
        token, project_lister=project_lister, profile_lister=profile_lister
    )
    for route in routes:
        if route.model == wanted:
            return route
    for route in routes:
        if route.profile_name == wanted:
            return route
        if f"{route.project_name}/{route.profile_name}" == wanted:
            return route
    raise OpenAIApiError(
        f"Profile '{wanted}' is not available for this token. See GET /v1/models.",
        status=404,
        code="model_not_found",
    )


def list_models(
    secret: str,
    *,
    store: Any = None,
    project_lister: Any = None,
    profile_lister: Any = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the OpenAI model list: the profiles this token can reach."""
    token = authorize(secret, store=store)
    data = [
        {
            "id": route.model,
            "object": "model",
            "created": 0,
            "owned_by": route.project_name or "codx-junior",
        }
        for route in allowed_routes(
            token, project_lister=project_lister, profile_lister=profile_lister
        )
    ]
    return {"object": "list", "data": data}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Messages
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def content_text(content: Any) -> str:
    """Flatten an OpenAI message ``content`` (string or parts) into text."""
    if content is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        parts: List[str] = []
        for item in content:
            if isinstance(item, str):
                parts.append(item)
            elif isinstance(item, dict):
                text = item.get("text")
                if not isinstance(text, str) and isinstance(item.get("content"), str):
                    text = item["content"]
                if isinstance(text, str):
                    parts.append(text)
        return "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
    return str(content)


def incoming_pairs(messages: Any) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    """
    Normalise the request ``messages`` into ``(role, content)`` pairs.

    Raises:
        OpenAIApiError: 400 when a message is not an object.
    """
    if not isinstance(messages, list):
        raise OpenAIApiError(
            "Field 'messages' must be a list of {role, content} objects.",
            status=400,
            code="messages_required",
        )
    pairs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    for message in messages:
        if not isinstance(message, dict):
            raise OpenAIApiError(
                "Every entry of 'messages' must be an object with role and content.",
                status=400,
                code="invalid_messages",
            )
        pairs.append(
            (str(message.get("role") or "user"), content_text(message.get("content")))
        )
    return pairs


def stored_pairs(chat: Any) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return the ``(role, content)`` pairs already persisted in a chat."""
    return [
        (str(getattr(message, "role", "") or ""), content_text(getattr(message, "content", "")))
        for message in (getattr(chat, "messages", None) or [])
    ]


def pending_pairs(
    stored: List[Tuple[str, str]], incoming: List[Tuple[str, str]]
) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    """
    Return the messages of *incoming* that are not stored yet.

    Clients send the whole history on every call, so the stored tail and the
    incoming head are aligned by the longest overlap. A client that sends only
    the new message has no overlap and everything is appended.
    """
    if not stored:
        return list(incoming)
    overlap = 0
    for size in range(min(len(stored), len(incoming)), 0, -1):
        if stored[len(stored) - size:] == incoming[:size]:
            overlap = size
            break
    return list(incoming[overlap:])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conversations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def find_conversation(
    conversation_id: str,
    token: Any,
    *,
    project_lister: Any = None,
    profile_lister: Any = None,
    session_factory: Any = None,
    prefer: Any = None,
) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[ProfileRoute]]:
    """
    Load a persisted conversation (a chat) among the projects the token allows.

    The project of the requested model is searched first, then the rest of the
    token's projects. A chat outside the token's projects is invisible.
    """
    wanted = str(conversation_id or "").strip()
    if not wanted:
        return None, None
    routes = allowed_routes(
        token, project_lister=project_lister, profile_lister=profile_lister
    )
    preferred_key = _project_key(prefer) if prefer is not None else ""
    ordered = sorted(
        routes, key=lambda route: 0 if _project_key(route.settings) == preferred_key else 1
    )
    visited = set()
    for route in ordered:
        key = _project_key(route.settings)
        if key in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(key)
        try:
            session = _session(route.settings, session_factory)
            chat = session.get_chat_manager().find_by_id(wanted)
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning("OpenAI API: cannot load chat %s: %s", wanted, ex)
            continue
        if chat is not None:
            return chat, route
    return None, None


def _chat_epoch(chat: Any, *, default: Optional[int] = None) -> int:
    for attribute in ("updated", "created", "created_at"):
        value = getattr(chat, attribute, None)
        if value is None:
            continue
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            return int(value)
        parsed = getattr(value, "timestamp", None)
        if callable(parsed):
            try:
                return int(parsed())
            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                continue
    return int(default if default is not None else time.time())


def conversation_payload(chat: Any, route: ProfileRoute) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Render a persisted chat as an OpenAI conversation (with its items)."""
    created = _chat_epoch(chat)
    messages = []
    items = []
    for index, message in enumerate(getattr(chat, "messages", None) or []):
        role = str(getattr(message, "role", "") or "user")
        text = content_text(getattr(message, "content", ""))
        messages.append({"role": role, "content": text})
        items.append(
            {
                "id": str(
                    getattr(message, "doc_id", "")
                    or getattr(message, "id", "")
                    or f"{chat.id}-{index}"
                ),
                "object": "conversation.item",
                "type": "message",
                "role": role,
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "output_text" if role == "assistant" else "input_text",
                        "text": text,
                    }
                ],
            }
        )
    return {
        "id": str(getattr(chat, "id", "") or ""),
        "object": "conversation",
        "created_at": created,
        "metadata": {
            "title": str(getattr(chat, "name", "") or ""),
            "model": route.model,
            "project": route.project_name,
            "profile": route.profile_name,
        },
        "model": route.model,
        "messages": messages,
        "data": items,
    }


def get_conversation(
    secret: str,
    conversation_id: str,
    *,
    store: Any = None,
    project_lister: Any = None,
    profile_lister: Any = None,
    session_factory: Any = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Recover a previous conversation by id.

    Raises:
        OpenAIApiError: 404 when the conversation does not exist in any project
            the token is allowed to use.
    """
    token = authorize(secret, store=store)
    chat, route = find_conversation(
        conversation_id,
        token,
        project_lister=project_lister,
        profile_lister=profile_lister,
        session_factory=session_factory,
    )
    if chat is None:
        raise OpenAIApiError(
            f"Conversation '{conversation_id}' was not found.",
            status=404,
            code="conversation_not_found",
        )
    return conversation_payload(chat, route)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Chat completion
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _new_chat(route: ProfileRoute, body: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    from codx.junior.db import Chat

    metadata = body.get("metadata") if isinstance(body.get("metadata"), dict) else {}
    title = str((metadata or {}).get("title") or "").strip()
    chat = Chat(
        name=title or f"{route.model} conversation",
        profiles=[route.profile_name],
        messages=[],
    )
    return chat


def _rough_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    return max(1, len(text or "") // 4) if text else 0


def completion_payload(
    route: ProfileRoute, chat: Any, *, now: Optional[int] = None
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Render the chat's last assistant message as an OpenAI chat completion."""
    messages = list(getattr(chat, "messages", None) or [])
    reply = ""
    for message in reversed(messages):
        if str(getattr(message, "role", "") or "") == "assistant":
            reply = content_text(getattr(message, "content", ""))
            break
    prompt_tokens = sum(
        _rough_tokens(content_text(getattr(message, "content", "")))
        for message in messages
        if str(getattr(message, "role", "") or "") != "assistant"
    )
    completion_tokens = _rough_tokens(reply)
    total_tokens = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens
    return {
        "id": f"chatcmpl-{getattr(chat, 'id', '') or ''}",
        "object": "chat.completion",
        "created": int(now if now is not None else time.time()),
        "model": route.model,
        "conversation_id": str(getattr(chat, "id", "") or ""),
        "choices": [
            {
                "index": 0,
                "message": {
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "content": reply,
                    "refusal": None,
                    "annotations": [],
                },
                "logprobs": None,
                "finish_reason": "stop",
            }
        ],
        "usage": {
            "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens,
            "completion_tokens": completion_tokens,
            "total_tokens": total_tokens,
        },
    }


async def chat_completion(
    secret: str,
    body: Any,
    *,
    store: Any = None,
    project_lister: Any = None,
    profile_lister: Any = None,
    session_factory: Any = None,
    now: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Serve one ``POST /v1/chat/completions``.

    The profile named in ``model`` (and granted by the token) serves the turn.
    ``conversation_id`` continues an existing conversation: the stored chat is
    reloaded, only the messages that are not persisted yet are appended, and
    the same id comes back in the answer.

    Raises:
        OpenAIApiError: 400/401/404 for invalid input, credentials or models and
            409 when the conversation belongs to another project than the model.
    """
    token = authorize(secret, store=store)
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        raise OpenAIApiError(
            "The request body must be a JSON object.", status=400, code="invalid_request"
        )
    route = resolve_route(
        token,
        body.get("model"),
        project_lister=project_lister,
        profile_lister=profile_lister,
    )
    incoming = incoming_pairs(body.get("messages"))
    if not incoming:
        raise OpenAIApiError(
            "Field 'messages' must be a non-empty list.", status=400, code="messages_required"
        )

    conversation_id = str(
        body.get("conversation_id") or body.get("conversationId") or ""
    ).strip()

    chat = None
    if conversation_id:
        chat, chat_route = find_conversation(
            conversation_id,
            token,
            project_lister=project_lister,
            profile_lister=profile_lister,
            session_factory=session_factory,
            prefer=route.settings,
        )
        if chat is None:
            raise OpenAIApiError(
                f"Conversation '{conversation_id}' was not found.",
                status=404,
                code="conversation_not_found",
            )
        if _project_key(chat_route.settings) != _project_key(route.settings):
            raise OpenAIApiError(
                f"Conversation '{conversation_id}' belongs to project "
                f"'{chat_route.project_name}', not to '{route.project_name}'.",
                status=409,
                code="conversation_project_mismatch",
            )
    if chat is None:
        chat = _new_chat(route, body)
    chat.profiles = [route.profile_name]

    from codx.junior.db import Message

    for role, content in pending_pairs(stored_pairs(chat), incoming):
        chat.messages.append(Message(role=role, content=content))

    session = _session(route.settings, session_factory)
    await session.chat_with_project(chat=chat)
    return completion_payload(route, chat, now=now)

"""
Tests for the global PATs and the OpenAI-compatible API.

Run with::

    PYTHONPATH=api python -m pytest api/tests/test_openai_pat_api.py -q

What is proven here:

* a PAT is GLOBAL: it stores no owner and only a digest of its secret;
* a PAT declares the profiles (models) it can reach, and the OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint routes the ``model`` field to that profile;
* a conversation survives between calls (``conversation_id``) and can be
  recovered (``GET /v1/conversations/{id}``) without duplicating its history.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from codx.junior import openai_api as service
from codx.junior.api import chatGPTLikeApi
from codx.junior.db import Chat, Message
from codx.junior.security import api_tokens as store


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fakes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class FakeProfile:
    def __init__(self, name, active=False, model_name=None, description=""):
        self.name = name
        self.description = description or f"{name} profile"
        self.api_settings = SimpleNamespace(
            active=active, model_name=model_name, description=None
        )


class FakeProject:
    def __init__(self, project_name, project_id, profiles):
        self.project_name = project_name
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.profiles = profiles


class FakeChatManager:
    def __init__(self, state):
        self.state = state

    def find_by_id(self, chat_id):
        return self.state["chats"].get(chat_id)


class FakeSession:
    """Minimal session: persists chats and answers with the routed profile."""

    def __init__(self, settings, state):
        self.settings = settings
        self.state = state

    def get_chat_manager(self):
        return FakeChatManager(self.state)

    async def chat_with_project(self, chat):
        self.state["calls"].append(chat)
        if not chat.id:
            chat.id = f"chat-{len(self.state['chats']) + 1}"
        profile = chat.profiles[0] if chat.profiles else "?"
        chat.messages.append(Message(role="assistant", content=f"reply by {profile}"))
        self.state["chats"][chat.id] = chat
        return chat, []


@pytest.fixture()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The PAT is global
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_token_is_global_and_only_its_digest_is_stored(token_db):
    token, secret = store.create_token(name="n8n workflow", profiles=["developer"])

    assert secret.startswith(store.TOKEN_PREFIX)
    assert token.token_hash == store.hash_token(secret)
    assert secret.endswith(token.token_hash) is False
    assert token.prefix == secret[: store.PREFIX_LENGTH]
    assert secret not in token.token_hash and secret not in token.prefix

    # No owner: a PAT is not tied to a user.
    assert not hasattr(token, "username")
    assert not hasattr(token, "user")

    view = store.public_view(token)
    assert "token" not in view and "token_hash" not in view
    assert view["profiles"] == ["developer"]

    # It lives in the global settings section, not in a project or a user.
    assert token_db["sections"]["api_tokens"][0]["id"] == token.id


def test_find_token_requires_a_live_global_token(token_db):
    token, secret = store.create_token(name="cli", profiles=["developer"])
    assert store.find_token(secret).id == token.id
    assert store.find_token("") is None
    assert store.find_token("cxj_pat_nope") is None

    store.update_token(token.id, enabled=False)
    assert store.find_token(secret) is None

    expired = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
    token2, secret2 = store.create_token(name="old", expires_at=expired)
    assert store.find_token(secret2) is None
    assert store.is_expired(token2)

    token3, secret3 = store.create_token(name="fresh")
    assert store.find_token(secret3).id == token3.id


def test_tokens_are_listed_and_revoked(token_db):
    first, _ = store.create_token(name="a")
    second, _ = store.create_token(name="b")
    assert [token.id for token in store.list_tokens()] == [first.id, second.id]

    store.update_token(first.id, name="a renamed", profiles=["developer"])
    assert store.get_token(first.id).name == "a renamed"
    assert store.get_token(first.id).profiles == ["developer"]

    assert store.delete_token(second.id) is True
    assert store.delete_token(second.id) is False
    assert [token.id for token in store.list_tokens()] == [first.id]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The PAT defines the models (profiles) it can reach
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_models_are_the_profiles_granted_to_the_token(world):
    _, granted = store.create_token(name="explicit", profiles=["developer"])
    assert [model["id"] for model in models(world, granted)["data"]] == ["demo/developer"]

    # A profile is also reachable by the name it publishes in api_settings.
    _, published = store.create_token(name="published", profiles=["coder-xl"])
    assert [model["id"] for model in models(world, published)["data"]] == ["coder-xl"]

    # No grant (or ['*']) means "everything already exposed through the API".
    _, exposed = store.create_token(name="all")
    assert [model["id"] for model in models(world, exposed)["data"]] == [
        "demo/developer",
        "coder-xl",
    ]

    # 'reviewer' is not exposed and not granted: it never appears.
    assert "demo/reviewer" not in [model["id"] for model in models(world, exposed)["data"]]

def test_chat_completion_routes_the_model_field_to_the_profile(world):
    _, secret = store.create_token(name="chat", profiles=["developer", "coder-xl"])

    payload = chat(
        world, secret, {"model": "developer", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}

request.content:
# OpenAI-compatible API (global PATs)

codx-junior exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint whose **routing unit is the
profile**: the client sends the profile name in the `model` field and the
request is served by that profile of that project.

```
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://<codx-junior-host>/api
OPENAI_API_KEY=cxj_pat_...
model=<profile>                 # or <project>/<profile>, or api_settings.model_name
```

> Base URL ends at `/api`: the routes are `/api/v1/models`,
> `/api/v1/chat/completions`, `/api/v1/conversations/{id}`.

## 1. PATs are global, never owned by a user

A personal access token is a **machine credential of the installation**
(`ApiToken` in the `api_tokens` section of the global settings):

* it stores no owner — it keeps working when the user who created it leaves,
  changes password or is disabled;
* only the SHA-256 **digest** of the secret is persisted, plus a short
  non-secret `prefix` so an admin can recognise it in a list;
* the secret is returned **once**, by `POST /api/api-tokens`;
* a token can be disabled, re-expired or revoked at any time, and every request
  re-checks it (`/api/v1/...` answers `401 invalid_api_key` otherwise).

## 2. The PAT declares the profiles it can reach

`profiles` on the token is the authorisation list. An entry is a profile name,
`<project>/<profile>` or the profile's `api_settings.model_name`.

| `profiles` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `["developer", "demo/reviewer"]` | exactly those profiles (an explicit grant wins over `api_settings.active`) |
| `[]` or `["*"]` | every profile already published through the API (`api_settings.active`) |

`GET /api/v1/models` returns **only** the models that token may use, so a client
cannot even see the rest. A model outside the grant answers
`404 model_not_found`.

## 3. Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/models` | profiles granted to the PAT |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/models/{model}` | one model (the profile) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/chat/completions` | chat; `model` = profile, SSE when `stream: true` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/completions` | legacy alias (`prompt` becomes the user message) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` | recover a previous conversation |

Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer cxj_pat_...` (the legacy `authentication`
header is accepted too).

## 4. Recovering a previous conversation

A conversation **is** the chat codx-junior already persists in the project, so
nothing extra is stored and the conversation shows up in the UI like any other
chat.

```bash
# 1) open a conversation
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CODEX_PAT" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"developer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
# -> { ..., "conversation_id": "4f2c..." }

# 2) continue it later (send the id back, with or without the history)
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CODEX_PAT" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"developer","conversation_id":"4f2c...","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"and then?"}]}'

# 3) read the stored transcript
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/v1/conversations/4f2c... -H "Authorization: Bearer $CODEX_PAT"
```

The answer always carries the id, in the body (`conversation_id`) and in the
`x-codx-conversation-id` header.

### Should we follow the OpenAI Conversations API?

Partly — and that is what is implemented:

* **Adopted**: the id-based contract. `conversation_id` on
  `chat/completions` is what every OpenAI-compatible client can round-trip, and
  `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` returns the Conversations-API shape
  (`object`, `created_at`, `metadata`, `data` items) so a client already written
  against that object can read it. A plain `messages` list is included for
  clients that just want role/content pairs.
* **Not adopted (yet)**: `POST /v1/conversations`, item-level CRUD
  (`/conversations/{id}/items`), truncation strategies and server-side item
  streaming. They add a second storage model next to the chat that already
  exists, and the value ("resume where I left off") is already covered.
  Conversation history duplication is avoided by aligning the stored tail with
  the incoming head, so a client that resends the whole history and a client
  that sends only the new message both work.

A conversation found in a different project than the one the `model` resolves to
is rejected with `409 conversation_project_mismatch` instead of silently mixing
two projects.

## 5. Admin endpoints

Admin session required (`require_admin`):

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/api-tokens` | list tokens (never a secret or a digest) |
| `GET` | `/api/api-tokens/profiles` | profiles that can be granted (`exposed` flag) |
| `POST` | `/api/api-tokens` | create; the `token` field is shown once |
| `PATCH` | `/api/api-tokens/{id}` | rename, re-grant, disable, re-expire |
| `DELETE` | `/api/api-tokens/{id}` | revoke immediately |

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/api-tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_SESSION" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"n8n workflow","profiles":["developer"],"description":"nightly triage"}'
```

## 6. Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=api python -m pytest api/tests/test_openai_pat_api.py -q
```

They prove: the secret is only stored as a digest, a token has no owner, the
model list is the token's grant, `model` routes the request to the profile,
`conversation_id` continues a conversation without duplicating its history and
`GET /v1/conversations/{id}` recovers it.

"""
Tests for the global PATs (``security/api_tokens.py``), the OpenAI-compatible
service (``openai_api.py``) and its HTTP surface (``api/chatGPTLikeApi.py``).

Run with::

    PYTHONPATH=api python -m pytest api/tests/test_api_tokens_openai_api_chatGPTLikeApi.py -q

What is proven here:

* a PAT is GLOBAL: it stores no owner and only a digest of its secret;
* a PAT declares the profiles (models) it can reach, and the OpenAI-compatible
  endpoint routes the ``model`` field to that profile;
* a conversation survives between calls (``conversation_id``) and can be
  recovered (``GET /v1/conversations/{id}``) without duplicating its history.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from codx.junior import openai_api as service
from codx.junior.api import chatGPTLikeApi
from codx.junior.db import Chat, Message
from codx.junior.security import api_tokens as store


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fakes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class FakeProfile:
    def __init__(self, name, active=False, model_name=None, description=""):
        self.name = name
        self.description = description or f"{name} profile"
        self.api_settings = SimpleNamespace(
            active=active, model_name=model_name, description=None
        )


class FakeProject:
    def __init__(self, project_name, project_id, profiles):
        self.project_name = project_name
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.profiles = profiles


class FakeChatManager:
    """Chat storage of ONE project, like the real per-project chat manager."""

    def __init__(self, state, project_id):
        self.state = state
        self.project_id = project_id

    def find_by_id(self, chat_id):
        return self.state["chats"].get(f"{self.project_id}:{chat_id}")


class FakeSession:
    """Minimal session: persists chats per project and answers with the profile."""

    def __init__(self, settings, state):
        self.settings = settings
        self.state = state
        self.project_id = settings.project_id

    def get_chat_manager(self):
        return FakeChatManager(self.state, self.project_id)

    async def chat_with_project(self, chat):
        self.state["calls"].append(chat)
        if not chat.id:
            self.state["seq"] += 1
            chat.id = f"chat-{self.state['seq']}"
        profile = chat.profiles[0] if chat.profiles else "?"
        chat.messages.append(Message(role="assistant", content=f"reply by {profile}"))
        self.state["chats"][f"{self.project_id}:{chat.id}"] = chat
        return chat, []


@pytest.fixture()
def token_db(monkeypatch):
    """In-memory replacement of the ``api_tokens`` settings section."""
    state = {"sections": {}}

    def read_global_settings(refresh=False):
        return SimpleNamespace(api_tokens=state["sections"].get("api_tokens", []))

    def write_settings_section(section, data):
        state["sections"][section] = data

    monkeypatch.setattr(store, "read_global_settings", read_global_settings)
    monkeypatch.setattr(store, "write_settings_section", write_settings_section)
    store._LAST_TOUCH.clear()
    return state


@pytest.fixture()
def world(token_db):
    state = {"chats": {}, "calls": [], "seq": 0}
    projects = {
        "p1": FakeProject(
            "demo",
            "proj-1",
            [FakeProfile("developer", active=True), FakeProfile("reviewer")],
        ),
        "p2": FakeProject(
            "other", "proj-2", [FakeProfile("coder", active=True, model_name="coder-xl")]
        ),
    }
    return SimpleNamespace(
        state=state,
        projects=projects,
        project_lister=lambda: projects,
        profile_lister=lambda settings: settings.profiles,
        session_factory=lambda settings: FakeSession(settings, state),
    )


def run(coro):
    return asyncio.run(coro)


def chat(world, secret, body):
    return run(
        service.chat_completion(
            secret,
            body,
            project_lister=world.project_lister,
            profile_lister=world.profile_lister,
            session_factory=world.session_factory,
        )
    )


def stored_chat(world, project_id, chat_id):
    return world.state["chats"][f"{project_id}:{chat_id}"]


def models(world, secret):
    return service.list_models(
        secret,
        project_lister=world.project_lister,
        profile_lister=world.profile_lister,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The PAT is global
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_token_is_global_and_only_its_digest_is_stored(token_db):
    token, secret = store.create_token(name="n8n workflow", profiles=["developer"])

    assert secret.startswith(store.TOKEN_PREFIX)
    assert token.token_hash == store.hash_token(secret)
    assert token.prefix == secret[: store.PREFIX_LENGTH]
    assert secret not in token.token_hash and secret not in token.prefix

    # No owner: a PAT is not tied to a user.
    assert not hasattr(token, "username")
    assert not hasattr(token, "user")

    view = store.public_view(token)
    assert "token" not in view and "token_hash" not in view
    assert view["profiles"] == ["developer"]

    # It lives in the global settings section, not in a project or a user.
    assert token_db["sections"]["api_tokens"][0]["id"] == token.id


def test_find_token_requires_a_live_global_token(token_db):
    token, secret = store.create_token(name="cli", profiles=["developer"])
    assert store.find_token(secret).id == token.id
    assert store.find_token("") is None
    assert store.find_token("cxj_pat_nope") is None

    store.update_token(token.id, enabled=False)
    assert store.find_token(secret) is None

    expired = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
    token2, secret2 = store.create_token(name="old", expires_at=expired)
    assert store.find_token(secret2) is None
    assert store.is_expired(token2)

    token3, secret3 = store.create_token(name="fresh")
    assert store.find_token(secret3).id == token3.id


def test_tokens_are_listed_and_revoked(token_db):
    first, _ = store.create_token(name="a")
    second, _ = store.create_token(name="b")
    assert [token.id for token in store.list_tokens()] == [first.id, second.id]

    store.update_token(first.id, name="a renamed", profiles=["developer"])
    assert store.get_token(first.id).name == "a renamed"
    assert store.get_token(first.id).profiles == ["developer"]

    assert store.delete_token(second.id) is True
    assert store.delete_token(second.id) is False
    assert [token.id for token in store.list_tokens()] == [first.id]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The PAT defines the models (profiles) it can reach
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```md docs/openai-compatible-api.md
# OpenAI-compatible API (global PATs)

codx-junior exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint whose **routing unit is the
profile**: the client sends the profile name in the `model` field and the
request is served by that profile of that project.

```
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://<codx-junior-host>/api
OPENAI_API_KEY=cxj_pat_...
model=<profile>                 # or <project>/<profile>, or api_settings.model_name
```

> Base URL ends at `/api`: the routes are `/api/v1/models`,
> `/api/v1/chat/completions`, `/api/v1/conversations/{id}`.

## 1. PATs are global, never owned by a user

A personal access token is a **machine credential of the installation**
(`ApiToken` in the `api_tokens` section of the global settings):

* it stores no owner — it keeps working when the user who created it leaves,
  changes password or is disabled;
* only the SHA-256 **digest** of the secret is persisted, plus a short
  non-secret `prefix` so an admin can recognise it in a list;
* the secret is returned **once**, by `POST /api/api-tokens`;
* a token can be disabled, re-expired or revoked at any time, and every request
  re-checks it (`/api/v1/...` answers `401 invalid_api_key` otherwise).

## 2. The PAT declares the profiles it can reach

`profiles` on the token is the authorisation list. An entry is a profile name,
`<project>/<profile>` or the profile's `api_settings.model_name`.

| `profiles` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `["developer", "demo/reviewer"]` | exactly those profiles (an explicit grant wins over `api_settings.active`) |
| `[]` or `["*"]` | every profile already published through the API (`api_settings.active`) |

`GET /api/v1/models` returns **only** the models that token may use, so a client
cannot even see the rest. A model outside the grant answers
`404 model_not_found`.

## 3. Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/models` | profiles granted to the PAT |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/models/{model}` | one model (the profile) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/chat/completions` | chat; `model` = profile, SSE when `stream: true` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/completions` | legacy alias (`prompt` becomes the user message) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}` | recover a previous conversation |

Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer cxj_pat_...` (the legacy `authentication`
header is accepted too).

## 4. Recovering a previous conversation

A conversation **is** the chat codx-junior already persists in the project, so
nothing extra is stored and the conversation shows up in the UI like any other
chat.

```bash
# 1) open a conversation
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CODEX_PAT" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"developer","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
# -> { ..., "conversation_id": "4f2c..." }

# 2) continue it later (send the id back, with or without the history)
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CODEX_PAT" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"developer","conversation_id":"4f2c...","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"and then?"}]}'

# 3) read the stored transcript
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/v1/conversations/4f2c... -H "Authorization: Bearer $CODEX_PAT"
```

The answer always carries the id, in the body (`conversation_id`) and in the
`x-codx-conversation-id` header.

### Should we follow the OpenAI Conversations API?

Partly — and that is what is implemented:

* **Adopted**: the id-based contract. `conversation_id` on
  `chat/completions` is what every OpenAI-compatible client can round-trip, and
  `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` returns the Conversations-API shape
  (`object`, `created_at`, `metadata`, `data` items) so a client already written
  against that object can read it. A plain `messages` list is included for
  clients that just want role/content pairs.
* **Not adopted (yet)**: `POST /v1/conversations`, item-level CRUD
  (`/conversations/{id}/items`), truncation strategies and server-side item
  streaming. They add a second storage model next to the chat that already
  exists, and the value ("resume where I left off") is already covered.
  Conversation history duplication is avoided by aligning the stored tail with
  the incoming head, so a client that resends the whole history and a client
  that sends only the new message both work.

A conversation found in a different project than the one the `model` resolves to
is rejected with `409 conversation_project_mismatch` instead of silently mixing
two projects.

## 5. Admin endpoints

Admin session required (`require_admin`):

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/api-tokens` | list tokens (never a secret or a digest) |
| `GET` | `/api/api-tokens/profiles` | profiles that can be granted (`exposed` flag) |
| `POST` | `/api/api-tokens` | create; the `token` field is shown once |
| `PATCH` | `/api/api-tokens/{id}` | rename, re-grant, disable, re-expire |
| `DELETE` | `/api/api-tokens/{id}` | revoke immediately |

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:19980/api/api-tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_SESSION" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"n8n workflow","profiles":["developer"],"description":"nightly triage"}'
```

## 6. Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=api python -m pytest api/tests/test_api_tokens_openai_api_chatGPTLikeApi.py -q
```

They prove: the secret is only stored as a digest, a token has no owner, the
model list is the token's grant, `model` routes the request to the profile,
`conversation_id` continues a conversation without duplicating its history and
`GET /v1/conversations/{id}` recovers it.

```
